Because the honest-dark script is already sitewide, this is a pure markup-lift: add the dispatch column to the propagate-nav footer template and re-propagate. Outcome: the owned-list capture surface goes from 1 page to every page, with zero new JS and zero new vendor.

items.summary: S186 lost a whole feature's telemetry to a silent bug: ignis-hint dispatched a vs:ux CustomEvent that no transport listened to, so every beacon was dropped. The real transport is a /v/rum sendBeacon gated by the Worker's RUM_UX_EVENTS allowlist — and there is NOTHING that keeps the emit call-sites in assets/*.js in sync with that allowlist. An emitted-but-unallowlisted name is silently discarded; an allowlisted-but-never-emitted name is dead config nobody notices.
items.why: This is the bug that already bit the studio once and will again — instrumentation that looks shipped but measures nothing is worse than no instrumentation, because it manufactures false confidence in a conversion surface. A structural gate that diffs the two sets turns a silent runtime drop into a loud build-time failure. Outcome: no RUM event the team adds can ever be silently dropped or left dead, protecting every funnel measurement the last three sessions built.
items.recipe: New scripts/check-rum-allowlist.mjs: parse RUM_UX_EVENTS from cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js; grep assets/*.js for emitUx('name')/sendBeacon('/v/rum'...) literal event names; report (a) emitted-but-not-allowlisted = ERROR (silent drop), (b) allowlisted-but-never-emitted = WARN (dead config). Include a --self-test with in-memory fixtures. Wire into build:check as advisory-then-strict.

items.summary: S187 built scripts/check-audit-staleness.mjs to grep the corpus for prior art before an audit scores an item — and it works (it caught 3 already-done items when dogfooded). But it is invoked only by hand, so the next agent that skips that step repeats the S186 waste of auditing already-shipped work. The freshness check is a script, not yet a gate.
items.why: A discipline that depends on the agent remembering to run it is a discipline that erodes — the only durable version is one the build enforces. Making freshness structural means every future audit in this repo inherits the prior-art check for free, regardless of which agent or skill produced it. Outcome: the 'already-done audit item' failure mode is closed at the plumbing level, not the habit level.
items.recipe: Extend scripts/check-audit-staleness.mjs to auto-discover the newest docs/AUDIT_*.json, extract each item's distinctive phrase from its summary/recipe, and grep TASK_BOARD DONE + the asset corpus; emit an advisory warning listing any item whose phrase already appears as shipped. Add it to the build:check chain (advisory). Document the call as the canonical pre-score step at the top of the audit JSON's generatedBy provenance.

items.summary: The S186 proof-conversion microline (assets/proof-conversion-line.js) renders an earned-trust line on the vault-member register card — but it ships completely blind: there is no emitUx call anywhere in the file, so its impression and click-through are unmeasurable. We cannot tell whether the proof line lifts register-card conversion or is wallpaper.
items.why: A conversion surface with no telemetry can never be tuned or killed — it just accretes. Adding two allowlisted RUM names (shown + click) makes the microline's lift observable in the same /v/rum stream as the rest of the funnel, so a future session can A/B or retire it on evidence. Outcome: the proof microline joins the measured funnel instead of being a faith-based UI element.
items.recipe: In assets/proof-conversion-line.js add an emitUx helper (mirror footer-dispatch.js's sendBeacon to /v/rum) firing 'proof-line:shown' when the line mounts (only when a real fresh proof renders) and 'proof-line:click' on the CTA link. Add both names to RUM_UX_EVENTS in cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js with a privacy comment. The new rum-allowlist gate (rank 2) will then verify both ends stay in sync.

items.summary: The top game detail pages read as catalog entries, not flagship pitches: hero + spec block + multiple competing links. The competitive leaders (one-product indie studios) give their flagship a narrative hero, one screenshot/loop, ONE primary CTA, and voice copy. With cross-game play-next now routing attention INTO these pages (S187), the pages they route into are the weak link.
items.why: Routing more attention into a page that does not convert just moves the bounce downstream. A focused storytelling pass on the single most-trafficked flagship — narrative hero, one decisive CTA, SOUL-voice copy, kill the competing links — tests the pattern before spending design budget on key art. Outcome: the destination of the play-next funnel earns the click it now receives.
items.recipe: Pick the highest-traffic live game detail page; restructure to narrative hero (one-line promise in SOUL voice) + single primary CTA (play / notify) + supporting proof, demote secondary links below the fold. No new key art (that is a founder/design commission — see blockedFounderGated). Ship one page as the template; defer the rest to a follow-up if time-bound.
